title: Pink Halloween Entryway Decor
description: Style a pink Halloween entryway with plain hot-pink pumpkins, black bats, gauze and LED lights, plus optional extras from your own home.
intro: A little pink, a little spooky, and a welcome worth opening the door for. Pretty Wicked pairs hot-pink pumpkins with a trail of black bats, soft gauze and two kinds of LED light. The contrast does the work: bright pink against a dark console, little faces glowing between the pumpkins, and folded wings leading your eye up the wall. Start with five finds and make the rest your own.

sections.heading: Pink pumpkins make the first impression
paragraphs: Choose the place you see as soon as the door opens: a console, shelf or small table already in your entryway. Put a few hot-pink pumpkins at one end, with a larger one toward the back and smaller shapes in front. The pumpkins in this selection are plain and uncarved. Their color is the statement; the little jack-o-lantern faces come from the separate light strand.

Leave a useful patch of surface beside the group. Keys still need somewhere to land, and a small entry does not need every piece from the seven-pumpkin set on display. A tight group at one end reads as an arrangement, while a pumpkin in every available gap can make the whole console feel crowded. Step back to the doorway and check what catches your eye first.

The flat-lay view shows the selected pieces before they move into the room. Use it to think about the balance of color: the pink pumpkins are the bold shapes, the black bats bring contrast, and the gauze and lights connect them. Confirm the actual pumpkin sizes and shade in the retailer's listing before planning your version.

sections.heading: A gauzy layer and a little jack-o-lantern glow
paragraphs: Slip the pink open-weave gauze beneath the pumpkin group and let a section fall over one edge. You want a loose, uneven drape that leaves some of the furniture visible. Gather the fabric beside the pumpkins instead of pulling it tightly across the entire console; the changes in texture are what make this layer feel Halloween-ready.

Thread a jack-o-lantern light strand around the front of the group, turning the little faces toward the room. The darker facial details give the pink-on-pink arrangement definition. In the styled scene, the lights sit among the pumpkins rather than becoming a separate straight line. If you use the second strand around a mirror, keep its battery pack secure and follow the manufacturer's placement instructions.

Add a few pink LED tea lights in the open gaps. Their white plastic flame tips provide the candle-like shape without real flames. Keep fabric, lights and wires clear of the doorway and away from anything that can catch when someone walks past. Check the gauze panel measurements and the actual strand length against your console before setting it up.

sections.heading: Let the bats take the pink up the wall
paragraphs: The black bat silhouettes give the display movement above the console. Start near the arrangement and build a loose rising trail, mixing a few sizes as you go. Fold the wings for dimension and vary the gaps rather than lining every bat up at the same distance. You can use a handful from the pack and still make the wall feel part of the scene.

If there is a mirror above your console, let the bats travel around one side of it. The mirror already gives the wall a focal point, so the silhouettes can frame it without covering everything. Look from the front door as well as straight on: the trail should connect to the pumpkins below, even when you see the entry at an angle.

The selected decorations are PVC silhouettes supplied with adhesive strips. Check whether the adhesive suits your wall finish before applying it, and follow the listing's directions. Keep the bats clear of hinges, locks and door hardware. A smaller arc is an easy option if your wall space is narrow or you want the mirror to stay more visible.

sections.heading: A welcome that belongs to your home
paragraphs: The porch view shows what visitors see when the door opens: the decorated console behind a real doorway moment, rather than a display cut off from the rest of the room. Use that view as your final styling check. Open the door fully, walk through the entry and make sure the draped gauze and light wires stay out of the path.

A bowl or basket you already own can hold wrapped treats. Borrow a vase, a small dish or a favorite frame from another room if you want a more collected arrangement. The console, mirror, flowers, artwork, mirror balls, candy cauldron and clothing in these images are styling extras. They are separate from the five selected finds and do not have to be recreated to get the pink-and-black effect.

For a compact version, keep the pumpkin group small and use one light strand with a short trail of bats above it. With more room, let the gauze fall a little farther and give the silhouettes a wider sweep. The same ingredients can work at either scale: a bold pink welcome, a little glow and enough space for everyday coming and going.
